questions.prompt: Which revision removes the ambiguous pronoun while preserving the original meaning that Elena planned to rehearse after meeting Jordan?
choices: After Elena met Jordan, Elena planned to rehearse for the audition.
After Elena met Jordan, she planned to rehearse for the audition.
After Elena met Jordan, she planned to rehearse for the audition because she wanted to impress the judges.
She planned to rehearse for the audition after meeting Jordan because she hoped the director would select her.
questions.explanation: Repeating Elena identifies the subject of planned without forcing the reader to decide which person she refers to.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the object-form relative pronoun after the verb praised?
choices: The student who the teacher praised received the highest score.
The student which the teacher praised received the highest score.
The student whom the teacher praised received the highest score.
The student whose the teacher praised received the highest score.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, whom is the object of praised, so it correctly refers to the student praised by the teacher.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: The manager sent the designer a message because she had misread the delivery date. Which revision makes clear that the manager, not the designer, had misread the date?
choices: The manager sent the designer a message because the manager had misread the delivery date.
The manager sent the designer a message because the designer had misread the delivery date.
The manager sent the designer a message because they had misread the delivery date.
The manager sent the designer a message because she had misread the delivery date.
questions.explanation: The correct revision repeats manager so that the pronoun she cannot be misread as referring to the designer.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly expresses the intended meaning that the panel did not adopt the motion and did not schedule another vote?
choices: The panel neither adopted the motion nor scheduled another vote.
The panel either did not adopt the motion or scheduled another vote.
The panel neither adopted the motion or scheduled another vote.
The panel not only failed to adopt the motion but also scheduled another vote.
questions.explanation: This revision uses the correlative pair neither and nor with parallel verbs to deny both actions unambiguously.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision clarifies that the book, not the student, concerns astronomy in this draft: The teacher handed the student a book about astronomy?
choices: The teacher handed the student a book that was about astronomy.
The teacher handed the student who studied astronomy a book.
The teacher handed the student a book about astronomy.
The teacher handed the student, a book about astronomy.
questions.explanation: This option uses a restrictive clause to make the book the clear subject of the phrase about astronomy.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which question correctly uses whom after the preposition to?
choices: To who did the committee award the scholarship?
To whom the committee awarded the scholarship?
To who the committee awarded the scholarship?
To whom did the committee award the scholarship?
questions.explanation: Whom is the objective case required after the preposition to, and did inversion makes the question grammatically complete.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses would rather followed by parallel bare infinitives?
choices: I would rather leave now than wait for the delayed bus.
I would rather to leave now than to wait for the delayed bus.
I would rather leaving now than waiting for the delayed bus.
I would rather leave now than to wait for the delayed bus.
questions.explanation: The modal would is followed here by the parallel bare infinitives leave and wait.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses a nonrestrictive clause to add information about why the bridge was closed?
choices: The bridge which was under repair remained closed all week.
The bridge, which was under repair, remained closed all week.
The bridge, which was under repair remained closed all week.
The bridge which was under repair, remained closed all week.
questions.explanation: The pair of commas correctly marks which was under repair as nonrestrictive information rather than a defining part of the subject.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the past perfect to report a completed observation that occurred before the witness spoke?
choices: The witness said that they have seen the suspect near the station at nine.
The witness said that they had seen the suspect near the station at nine.
The witness said that they had see the suspect near the station at nine.
The witness said that they saw the suspect near the station at nine.
questions.explanation: Had seen is the past perfect and places the witness's observation before the later act of speaking.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision corrects the faulty parallelism in the sentence The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and giving us feedback?
choices: The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and gave us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and giving us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and to give us feedback.
questions.explanation: This revision keeps all three coordinated verbs in the same simple past-tense form, so the list is properly parallel.
questions.skill: Correcting faulty parallelism in a compound predicate
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision makes the list parallel while preserving the present tense in this draft: The website lists volunteer opportunities, offers résumé templates, and giving interview advice?
choices: The website lists volunteer opportunities, offers résumé templates, and provides interview advice.
The website lists volunteer opportunities, offers résumé templates, and giving interview advice.
The website is listing volunteer opportunities, offers résumé templates, and provides interview advice.
The website lists volunteer opportunities, offered résumé templates, and provides interview advice.
questions.explanation: This option gives all three verbs the same present-tense form and preserves the website as the subject of each action.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses used to to express a former habit in the sentence When Priya first lived in the city, she was used to walk home at night, but she no longer lives there?
choices: When Priya first lived in the city, she used to walk home at night, but she no longer lives there.
When Priya first lived in the city, she used to walking home at night, but she no longer lives there.
When Priya first lived in the city, she was used to walking home at night, but she no longer lives there.
When Priya first lived in the city, she is used to walk home at night, but she no longer lives there.
questions.explanation: Used to followed by an infinitive expresses a former habit that no longer holds.
questions.skill: Used to and be used to
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision turns the passive, noun-heavy draft into a clear active sentence without changing its meaning: The decision was made after a long deliberation by the committee.
choices: After the committee deliberated for a long time, the decision was made by the group.
After a long deliberation, the committee made the decision.
After a long deliberation was made, the committee decided the outcome.
The committee's decision was made after a long deliberation by the members.
questions.explanation: The active construction identifies the committee as the agent and removes unnecessary passive phrasing while preserving the meaning that the committee reached its decision after extended discussion.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly attaches the introductory participial phrase to the people watching the waves without changing the intended action?
choices: Running along the shoreline, the joggers watched the waves erode the sandbank.
Running along the shoreline, the waves eroded the sandbank.
Running along the shoreline, the joggers saw the sandbank eroding.
Running along the shoreline, the waves were watched by the joggers as they eroded.
questions.explanation: This revision makes the joggers the subject of the introductory participial phrase and preserves the intended action of the waves eroding the sandbank.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9 (quiz/game): Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision expresses the mixed conditional meaning that the warning failed to arrive in time, but we are still leaving the building now?
choices: If the warning had reached us, we would leave the building now.
If the warning had reached us, we would have left the building then.
If the warning reached us, we would have left the building now.
If the warning would have reached us, we would leave the building now.
questions.explanation: The unreal past condition had reached pairs with the present result would leave to describe a present consequence of an unreal past event.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the subjunctive to express the director's demand that every member submit a proposal by Friday?
choices: The director insisted that every member submitted a proposal by Friday.
The director insisted that every member would submit a proposal by Friday.
The director insisted that every member submit a proposal by Friday.
The director insisted that every member submits a proposal by Friday.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive takes the bare form submit after insisted that, expressing the director's demand for each member's action.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly repairs the punctuation in this draft: The lead engineer a specialist in earthquake-resistant design presented the plans to the city council?
choices: The lead engineer, a specialist in earthquake-resistant design, presented the plans to the city council.
The lead engineer, a specialist in earthquake-resistant design presented the plans to the city council.
The lead engineer a specialist in earthquake-resistant design, presented the plans to the city council.
The lead engineer; a specialist in earthquake-resistant design; presented the plans to the city council.
questions.explanation: This option correctly sets off the appositive that renames the lead engineer with a matching pair of commas.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the correlative pair not only and but also with parallel verbs and standard punctuation?
choices: The proposal not only reducing costs but also improves worker safety.
The proposal not only reduces costs but also improving worker safety.
The proposal not only reduce costs but also improves worker safety.
The proposal not only reduces costs but also improves worker safety.
questions.explanation: The verbs reduces and improves are parallel in form, and not only and but also correctly pair the two ideas without a comma between them.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the preposition to with a gerund in the sentence The volunteers look forward to organizing the event before the festival?
choices: The volunteers look forward to organizing the event before the festival.
The volunteers look forward to organize the event before the festival.
The volunteers look forward to an organizing the event before the festival.
The volunteers look forward to the organizing the event before the festival.
questions.explanation: The phrasal expression look forward to takes a gerund because the word to functions as a preposition in this construction.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision uses not as...as to express that the newer model is not equally as quiet as the previous model?
choices: The newer model is not as quiet as the previous model.
The newer model is not as quieter as the previous model.
The newer model is not so quiet as the previous model.
The newer model is not as quiet than the previous model.
questions.explanation: The construction not as...as correctly states that the newer model does not match the previous model's quietness.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision best expresses the intended contrast between clear instructions and the mistakes that nevertheless occurred?
choices: Although the instructions were clear, we still made few mistakes.
Although the instructions were clear, we still made several mistake.
Although the instructions were clear, we still made several mistakes.
Although the instruction were clear, we still made several mistakes.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast between two true statements, and the plural forms instructions and mistakes agree with their subjects.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision applies the standard reported-speech shifts to both the future modal and the time expression in Ms. Patel's statement that she will review the proposal tomorrow?
choices: Ms. Patel said that she would review the proposal the next day.
Ms. Patel said that she will review the proposal tomorrow.
Ms. Patel said that she would review the proposal tomorrow.
Ms. Patel said that she will review the proposal the next day.
questions.explanation: Standard reported speech changes will to would and shifts tomorrow to the next day when the statement is reported after the original utterance.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision places the adjectives in the standard English order?
choices: The carpenter built a lovely small red Japanese wooden table.
The carpenter built a small lovely red Japanese wooden table.
The carpenter built a lovely small red wooden Japanese table.
The carpenter built a wooden small lovely Japanese red table.
questions.explanation: English generally orders adjectives as opinion, size, color, origin, material, and purpose or type, which this revision follows.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses a colon to introduce a list of three parallel sources of pollution?
choices: The study identified three sources of pollution; industrial waste, vehicle exhaust, and runoff from farms.
The study identified three sources of pollution, industrial waste, vehicle exhaust, and runoff from farms.
The study identified three sources of pollution: industrial waste, vehicle exhaust, and that runoff from farms.
The study identified three sources of pollution: industrial waste, vehicle exhaust, and runoff from farms.
questions.explanation: A colon properly introduces the three parallel noun phrases, and the final comma separates the last item in the list.
questions.skill: Revising colon usage and list parallelism
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses subject-verb inversion after the fronted phrase only after?
choices: Only the match began after the rain stopped.
Only after the rain stopped did the match begin.
Only after the rain stopped the match began.
Only after did the rain stopped the match begin.
questions.explanation: Fronting only after creates negative emphasis and requires inversion of the subject and verb, yielding did the match begin.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision preserves the restrictive meaning that only the students who studied for the exam passed?
choices: The students whom had studied for the exam passed.
The students who had studied for the exam passed.
The students, who had studied for the exam, passed.
The students who had studied, for the exam passed.
questions.explanation: Because the relative clause is not set off by commas, it restricts the reference to the subset of students who studied and passed.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses so with an adjective to introduce a result clause?
choices: The snow was so deep that it blocked the road.
The snow was such deep that it blocked the road.
The snow was so much deep that it blocked the road.
The snow was so deeply that it blocked the road.
questions.explanation: The intensifier so takes the adjective deep and introduces the result clause that it blocked the road.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision makes all three coordinated verbs agree in tense and presents the actions as a completed sequence?
choices: The researcher opened the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opens the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opened the archive, consult the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opening the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
questions.explanation: The three parallel clauses use past-tense verbs consistently, which matches the completed sequence of actions.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision uses a colon to introduce the explanation of the unexpected conclusion without changing the meaning: The restoration had accelerated rather than slowed the river's flow, so the conclusion was unexpected.
choices: The conclusion was unexpected, the restoration had accelerated rather than slowed the river's flow.
The conclusion was unexpected that the restoration had accelerated rather than slowed the river's flow.
The conclusion was unexpected; the restoration had accelerated rather than slowed the river's flow.
The conclusion was unexpected: the restoration had accelerated rather than slowed the river's flow.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly introduces the restoration's effect as an explanation of why the conclusion was unexpected.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision makes the verb tenses consistent in the sentence The documentary explains the history of the river and show how it shaped the town?
choices: The documentary explained the history of the river and showed how it shaped the town.
The documentary explains the history of the river and showed how it shaped the town.
The documentary explained the history of the river and will show how it shaped the town.
The documentary explains the history of the river and had shown how it shaped the town.
questions.explanation: Changing both coordinated verbs to the past tense gives the sentence a single consistent time frame.
questions.skill: Maintaining consistent tense across coordinated verbs
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision corrects the comma splice while preserving the original meaning that the committee approved the proposal and the members believed it would improve attendance?
choices: The committee approved the proposal. The members believed it would improve attendance.
The committee approved the proposal, the members believed it would improve attendance.
Approved the proposal, the committee members believed it would improve attendance.
The committee approved the proposal because the members believed it would improve attendance.
questions.explanation: Using a full stop creates two complete sentences and preserves the fact that the committee's approval and the members' belief are separate actions.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly expresses the doctor's recommendation in the subjunctive mood and keeps the actions parallel: The doctor recommended that the patient rest for two days and drink plenty of water.
choices: The doctor recommended that the patient rested for two days and drank plenty of water.
The doctor recommended that the patient to rest for two days and drink plenty of water.
The doctor recommended that the patient resting for two days and drinking plenty of water.
The doctor recommended that the patient rest for two days and drink plenty of water.
questions.explanation: A recommendation takes the subjunctive form rest and drink, with parallel bare infinitives expressing the two recommended actions.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision fixes the dangling modifier in the sentence Walking into the classroom, the bell rang loudly?
choices: Walking into the classroom, the student heard the bell ring loudly.
Walking into the classroom, the bell rang loudly.
Walking into the classroom, the student heard the bell rang loudly.
Walking into the classroom, the bell was heard by the student.
questions.explanation: This revision makes the person who is walking the subject of the main clause, so the introductory phrase logically modifies the student.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision completes the sentence with consistent subject-verb agreement and a grammatically parallel modifier: The committee, consisting of twelve members, ___ ready to begin.
choices: The committee, consist of twelve members, is ready to begin.
The committee consisting of twelve members, is ready to begin.
The committee, consisting of twelve members, are ready to begin.
The committee, consisting of twelve members, is ready to begin.
questions.explanation: In this context, the singular committee is treated as one unit, so is agrees with it, and consisting of correctly modifies the noun phrase.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses an absolute construction to describe what accompanies the players as they leave the field?
choices: With the final whistle blowing, the players left the field.
Despite the final whistle blowing, the players left the field.
Besides the final whistle blowing, the players left the field.
Between the final whistle blowing, the players left the field.
questions.explanation: With followed by a noun and a present participle forms an absolute construction that adds an accompanying circumstance.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly expresses the third conditional that the hikers would not have reached the summit if they had not packed enough water?
choices: If the hikers did not pack enough water, they would not reach the summit.
If the hikers had not packed enough water, they would not reach the summit.
If the hikers would not have packed enough water, they had not reached the summit.
If the hikers had not packed enough water, they would not have reached the summit.
questions.explanation: A third conditional pairs the past perfect had not packed with the conditional perfect would not have reached to describe an unrealized past outcome.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the future perfect to show one action completed before a future deadline?
choices: By Friday, the volunteers will have removed every fallen tree.
By Friday, the volunteers will remove every fallen tree.
By Friday, the volunteers will have removing every fallen tree.
By Friday, the volunteers will removed every fallen tree.
questions.explanation: The future perfect will have removed places the completion of the action before the future deadline of Friday.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses between for two named individuals and among for a larger group?
choices: The disagreement was between Elena and Omar, while the final decision rested between the judges.
The disagreement was among Elena and Omar, while the final decision rested among the judges.
The disagreement was between Elena and Omar, while the final decision rested among the judges.
The disagreement was among Elena and Omar, while the final decision rested between the judges.
questions.explanation: Between is correctly used for the two named individuals, and among is correctly used for the judges as a group.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses the causative have with a bare infinitive to express making someone perform an action?
choices: The supervisor made the team to submit the report twice.
The supervisor had the team submitted the report twice.
The supervisor made the team submitted the report twice.
The supervisor had the team submit the report twice.
questions.explanation: The causative have takes a bare infinitive, so had the team submit means the supervisor made the team submit the report.
questions.topic: Activity 6 of 9: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly uses a perfect modal to express a past action that was possible but did not happen in this draft: The team could of submitted the application before the deadline?
choices: The team could have submitted the application before the deadline.
The team could of submitted the application before the deadline.
The team could have submit the application before the deadline.
The team could had submitted the application before the deadline.
questions.explanation: This option correctly pairs the modal could with have and a past participle to express an unrealized past possibility.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision corrects subject-verb agreement in the sentence The box of old photographs are in the attic?
choices: The box of old photographs is in the attic.
The box of old photographs are in the attic.
The box of old photographs were in the attic.
The box of old photographs have been in the attic.
questions.explanation: The true subject is the singular noun box, so the verb must be the singular is regardless of the plural photographs inside the prepositional phrase.
questions.skill: Subject-verb agreement with an intervening prepositional phrase
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly joins the two independent clauses with a semicolon and properly punctuated conjunctive adverb?
choices: The train was delayed, consequently, we missed the connection.
The train was delayed consequently; we missed the connection.
The train was delayed; consequently, we missed the connection.
The train was delayed; consequently we missed the connection.
questions.explanation: The semicolon separates the two independent clauses, and the comma after consequently correctly links the second clause to the first.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly agrees the verb with the neither...nor construction while preserving the past meaning?
choices: Neither the printed instructions nor the online video guide was enough to solve the problem.
Neither the printed instructions nor the online video guide were enough to solve the problem.
Neither the printed instructions nor the online video guide have been enough to solve the problem.
Neither the printed instructions nor the online video guide is enough to solve the problem.
questions.explanation: With a neither...nor construction, the singular verb was agrees with the construction while preserving the original past meaning.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision uses a wh-cleft to emphasize the result rather than the people who experienced it: The sudden recovery surprised the medical team.
choices: What the medical team was surprised was the sudden recovery.
What surprised was the medical team's sudden recovery.
What surprised the medical team was the sudden recovery.
What was the sudden recovery that surprised the medical team.
questions.explanation: This wh-cleft places the sudden recovery after the linking verb was, emphasizing the result while retaining the medical team in the subordinate clause.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision uses an it-cleft to emphasize the event that the scholarship enabled Maya to attend?
choices: It was the summer program that the scholarship enabled Maya to attend.
It was the scholarship that enabled Maya to attend the summer program.
It was the summer program that the scholarship enabled Maya to attending.
It was the summer program that the scholarship enabled Maya for attending.
questions.explanation: The it-cleft construction in this option foregrounds the summer program as what the scholarship enabled Maya to attend.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Under the standard rule requiring a comma after a short introductory dependent clause, which revision correctly punctuates this draft: When the bell rang students closed their laptops?
choices: When the bell rang, students closed their laptops.
When the bell rang students, closed their laptops.
When the bell rang; students closed their laptops.
When the bell, rang students closed their laptops.
questions.explanation: This option correctly places a comma after the introductory clause When the bell rang.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision corrects the dangling modifier in the sentence After reviewing the notes, the test seemed easier to me?
choices: After I reviewed the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
After reviewing the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
Having reviewed the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
The test, after reviewing the notes, seemed easier to me.
questions.explanation: Making I the subject of the introductory subordinate clause means that the speaker, rather than the test, performs the action of reviewing.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision correctly distinguishes the transitive verb raise from the intransitive verb rise in the sentence At sunrise, the crew raise the flag and watches it raise in the wind?
choices: At sunrise, the crew raises the flag and watches it rise in the wind.
At sunrise, the crew rises the flag and watches it raise in the wind.
At sunrise, the crew raises the flag and watches it raise in the wind.
At sunrise, the crew raising the flag and watches it rise in the wind.
questions.explanation: Transitive raise takes the flag as its object, while intransitive rise describes the flag's upward motion without taking an object.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision turns the fragment Waiting for the results into a complete sentence without changing the meaning that the analysts are waiting for the results?
choices: The results were waiting for the analysts.
After the analysts had waited for the results.
The analysts were waiting for the results.
The analysts were waiting, and the results had arrived.
questions.explanation: The revised sentence uses the analysts as the subject and were waiting as the finite verb while preserving the original waiting relationship.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

questions.prompt: Which revision uses inversion to emphasize the close timing while preserving the meaning of the original sentence: The delegation had hardly arrived when the meeting began.
choices: Hardly the delegation had arrived when the meeting began.
Hardly had the delegation arrived when the meeting began.
Hardly had the delegation arrived before the meeting began.
Hardly had the delegation arrived when began the meeting.
questions.explanation: Fronting hardly triggers subject-auxiliary inversion, and when preserves the original close timing between the delegation's arrival and the meeting's start.
questions.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

feedback.correct: Sharp revision! Your snake slides on with stronger grammar.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite — that sentence still has a grammatical flaw. Look again before the next run.

feedback.lose: The run is over. Study the explanations and try another run to sharpen your revisions.

kept.prompt: Which revision corrects the comma splice while preserving the original meaning that the committee approved the proposal and the members believed it would improve attendance?
choices: The committee approved the proposal. The members believed it would improve attendance.
The committee approved the proposal, the members believed it would improve attendance.
Approved the proposal, the committee members believed it would improve attendance.
The committee approved the proposal because the members believed it would improve attendance.
kept.explanation: Using a full stop creates two complete sentences and preserves the fact that the committee's approval and the members' belief are separate actions.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

kept.prompt: Which revision removes the ambiguous pronoun while preserving the original meaning that Elena planned to rehearse after meeting Jordan?
choices: After Elena met Jordan, Elena planned to rehearse for the audition.
After Elena met Jordan, she planned to rehearse for the audition.
After Elena met Jordan, she planned to rehearse for the audition because she wanted to impress the judges.
She planned to rehearse for the audition after meeting Jordan because she hoped the director would select her.
kept.explanation: Repeating Elena identifies the subject of planned without forcing the reader to decide which person she refers to.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

kept.prompt: Which revision makes all three coordinated verbs agree in tense and presents the actions as a completed sequence?
choices: The researcher opened the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opens the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opened the archive, consult the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
The researcher opening the archive, consulted the oldest map, and recorded its location in the notebook.
kept.explanation: The three parallel clauses use past-tense verbs consistently, which matches the completed sequence of actions.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

kept.prompt: Which revision corrects the dangling modifier in the sentence After reviewing the notes, the test seemed easier to me?
choices: After I reviewed the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
After reviewing the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
Having reviewed the notes, the test seemed easier to me.
The test, after reviewing the notes, seemed easier to me.
kept.explanation: Making I the subject of the introductory subordinate clause means that the speaker, rather than the test, performs the action of reviewing.
kept.topic: Revise a Weak Sentence - Advanced Grammar Review

kept.prompt: Which revision corrects the faulty parallelism in the sentence The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and giving us feedback?
choices: The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and gave us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and giving us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and us feedback.
The coach explained the rules, demonstrated the drills, and to give us feedback.
kept.explanation: This revision keeps all three coordinated verbs in the same simple past-tense form, so the list is properly parallel.
